title: mrpipeline Developer Guide
text: R/plot.R also defines three plain exported functions (S3 methods – none forest_plot()’s list--mr_result input, outcome_forest_plot()’s table_forest_plot()’s caller-built data frame input fit plot(x, ...) dispatch): forest_plot(results, methods, relabel, ...) – one row per method. Filters reorders result’s $results methods, binds (list order becomes section order results named list), calls TwoSampleMR::forest_plot_1_to_many() TraitM = "method". Default methods puts "IVW (fixed effects)" "Inverse variance weighted"; relabel argument (default: rename "Inverse variance weighted" "IVW (random effects)") applied combined data’s method column filtering/ordering, never affects matching raw labels run_mr() produced. outcome_forest_plot(mr_res, xlab, method, colour_by, shape_by, ...) – one row per outcome. Standalone ggplot2 code rather forest_plot_1_to_many() wrapper, function force-blanks exposure column internally map colour shape grouping variable. method plain inclusion filter (priority/fallback selector): pass one label one model, get two rows outcome computed. colour_by/shape_by map arbitrary column mr_res aesthetic, e.g. instrument type model (fixed/random effects) can shown without colliding. Implementation note anyone extending outcome_forest_plot(): mapping always includes group = .data$method, even method isn’t mapped colour shape. makes ggplot2::position_dodge() separate two rows share outcome (e.g. fixed-effects random-effects estimate outcome) instead fully overplotting – removing group binding silently break dodge callers map colour_by/shape_by something method. table_forest_plot(dat, null_value, xlab, box_colour) – one row per outcome, rendered inline result/CI/p-value table alongside plotted estimate, via (Suggests-) forestplot package rather ggplot2. Ported project-level script (NLRP3/Lanyue_forestplot_script/build_cardiometabolic_forestplot.R) deliberate one-exception outcome_forest_plot()’s usual convention. Unlike original script, function never opens graphics device (internal pdf()/dev.()) – returns forestplot object, matching every plot function file behaves; caller renders via plot()/print() controls output device.

title: mrpipeline User Guide
text: running many parallel jobs (e.g. HPC cluster), PLINK’s default behaviour auto-detecting available threads memory can cause problems — worker may try reserve half node’s RAM. Use plink_threads plink_memory cap resource usage per call. can set per-call, via R options, via environment variables: Priority order: explicit argument > R option > environment variable > PLINK auto-detect (NULL). parameters available run_coloc().
code: # Per-call (highest priority) result <- run_mr(   exposure = exposure_data, exposure_id = "CD40",   outcome = outcome_data, outcome_id = "SjD",   bfile = "/path/to/ld_ref",   plink_threads = 1,   plink_memory = 2000 )  # Via R options (apply to all subsequent calls in the session) options(   mrpipeline.plink_threads = 1,   mrpipeline.plink_memory = 2000 )  # Via environment variables (e.g. in .Renviron or a job script) -- set # MRPIPELINE_PLINK_THREADS to 1 and MRPIPELINE_PLINK_MEMORY to 2000

Fixed effects listed random effects default, "Inverse variance weighted" relabelled "IVW (random effects)" display: Pass named list section several results one figure – e.g. primary analysis alongside positive negative controls: outcome_forest_plot() instead shows one row per outcome, one IVW model variants, optionally coloured /shaped grouping column attach (e.g. instrument used). title: Align harmonised data to an LD matrix, correcting allele orientation — align_to_ld_matrix
text: compute_ld_matrix()'s ld matrix signed relative reference panel's , arbitrary A1 allele (ld_matrix$alleles$ld_a1), need match harmonised_data$effect_allele.exposure. coloc.abf() unaffected (never uses LD, SNP's Bayes factor depends beta^2, per-SNP sign flip changes nothing), runsusie() fits joint model across SNPs LD beta/varbeta together – inconsistent sign even subset SNPs produces internally incoherent fit, susie_rss()'s check_prior safety check ("estimated prior variance unreasonably large" error) exists catch. Rather mutating harmonised_data$beta.exposure/beta.outcome directly (columns, accompanying allele-label columns, also used reporting/instrument export elsewhere keep reflecting true exposure-outcome harmonisation), returns ld_sign vector +1/-1 multiplied beta vectors constructing dataset_exp/dataset_out lists passed coloc::runsusie() (see run_coloc()). SNPs whose alleles match reference panel's A1/A2 (e.g. indels, multi-allelic mismatches) dropped returned data LD matrix. Palindromic SNPs (/T, C/G) EAF ambiguous zone (0.42-0.58, either exposure outcome) also dropped, since allele-identity matching alone distinguish "strand" "opposite strand, coincidentally two letters" – mirrors equivalent safety filter reference single-cell coloc pipeline (harmonise_for_coloc() single_cell_MR_IMID/SSZ_scMR_scripts/Scripts/scMR_onek1k_1M_coloc.R) motivated fix.

User entries checked built-list. bim_path Character. Path PLINK bfile prefix (without .bim) used recover rsIDs data lacks (joins chr + pos), recover chr/pos data rsIDs positional columns (joins rsID) – see rsID lookup bim file chr/pos lookup bim file (reverse direction). title: Format GWAS summary statistics to a standard schema — format_gwas
text: GWAS files (particularly older EBI deposits) report effect sizes odds ratios rather log-odds. beta absent – present entirely NA (GWAS Catalog templates carry empty beta column alongside populated odds_ratio column, e.g. Ji 2016 PSC) – column normalisation, column present, function automatically derives: beta = log() (natural log; converts log-odds scale MR requires) se = |beta| / qnorm(pval / 2) (Z-score back-calculation p-value) Z-score method requires pval present accurate effect sizes small (close 1), typical common-variant GWAS. informative message emitted whenever conversion applied. file column non-standard name, add via col_map = list(= "MY_OR_COLUMN").

title: Format GWAS summary statistics to a standard schema — format_gwas
text: GWAS files (typically METAL output) report Z-score rather beta/se – e.g. Hysi 2020 refractive error, strabismus, Cuellar-Partida 2021 handedness. beta absent column normalisation zscore column present, function derives automatically: se already present: beta = zscore * se. Otherwise, se first derived allele frequency sample size via standard GWAS Z-score formula, beta = zscore * se: se = 1 / sqrt(2 * eaf * (1 - eaf) * (n + zscore^2)). path requires eaf n columns. informative message emitted whenever conversion applied. file Z-score column non-standard name, add via col_map = list(zscore = "MY_Z_COLUMN"); likewise use col_map non-standard sample-size column (e.g. METAL's Weight), via col_map = list(n = "Weight").

See examples. xlab X-axis label. method Character vector method values include. Default c("Inverse variance weighted", "IVW (fixed effects)") includes wherever computed. Outcomes lacking requested method simply contribute row – silent substitution. relabel Named character vector, c(old = new), applied method column display, reads sensibly colour_by shape_by "method". "beta" plots linear effect-size scale: b_col/se_col (CI derived internally b \eqn{\pm} 1.96*se) linear x-axis reference line 0. Required columns depend choice – 3 columns required scale="", 2 beta/SE columns scale="beta". or_col, or_lci_col, or_uci_col Column names use point estimate 95% CI scale="".
